subject.title: fix(agents): expose fs discovery tools to codex

question: Should `group:fs` deliberately grant native `grep`, `find`, and `ls` discovery capabilities to coding and embedded Codex runs, including sandboxed runs, after the branch is rebased onto current main?
rationale: This is a valid-looking fix but expands a policy and sandbox capability boundary for existing configurations; code review cannot determine the intended permanent permission model without maintainer direction.

options.title: Accept discovery in group:fs
options.body: Rebase the PR, retain the sandbox-aware implementation, and approve `grep`, `find`, and `ls` as standard filesystem-group capabilities.

options.title: Keep group:fs narrower
options.body: Do not expose discovery tools through the existing group until maintainers define a separate opt-in policy group or configuration path.

options.title: Adopt a smaller core seam
options.body: Land only a generic sandbox discovery seam if needed, while leaving policy exposure to a separately approved owner change.

recommendation.title: Accept discovery in group:fs
recommendation.body: Rebase the PR, retain the sandbox-aware implementation, and approve `grep`, `find`, and `ls` as standard filesystem-group capabilities.

likelyOwner.reason: The available timeline shows direct involvement when the initial security-boundary review was routed, but repository-history confirmation is unavailable in this run.
